title: Backward sweep writes a tape zone
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state machine over $\Gamma$, let $a_0\in\Gamma$, and let $c$ be a configuration on an input word $y$. Choose a state $q$, an optional input symbol $\mathit{inp}$, a table $\mathit{reads}$ of optional symbols, integers $a,z$, a natural number $n$, an enlarged-alphabet input $x$ with head position $p$, an output word $\mathit{out}$, and finite stacks $l,r$. Starting from the backward-sweep configuration at frontier $z$ whose right stack is the reversed list of the $n$ consecutive tape blocks of $c$ beginning at $a$, each encoded as a sweep symbol, followed by $r$, after $nk$ steps the simulator is at frontier $z-nk$. Its left stack is the list of the corresponding $n$ blocks of the configuration obtained by applying $M$'s transition at $(q,\mathit{inp},\mathit{reads})$, encoded as sweep symbols and prepended to $l$; its right stack remains $r$, and its state, input position, and output are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: enlarged-alphabet input $x$ and valid input-head position $p$
